messages:
priya: quick question about embeddings API behavior — mixing input types and truncation across auto-splitting. example payload i'm testing:
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-3-small",
  "inputs": [
    "short string",
    "a very long document... (10k chars)",
    {"blob": "base64:..."},
    []
  ]
}
```
What should clients expect for: accepted input types, per-item truncation rules, how we split/return batches, and the output vector shape for empty/invalid items? pinging @jamal for contract details (also mentioned in PR 542).

jamal: TL;DR: supported input is plain string for text items. If you're sending raw binary, encode as base64 string and label it in your client — server doesn't accept binary payloads directly. We don't accept token arrays or nested lists as a typed input.

jamal: truncation & splitting: truncation is applied per-item before batching (we truncate each text item to 4096 characters by default for embed-3-small; this maps roughly to the model's token safety cap). If a single item exceeds that we cut at 4096 chars and still return one embedding for that item. If the request contains many items and the internal compute batch size would be breached, we internally split the request into compute batches but preserve the input order on return.

alex: to add: max items per HTTP request is 2048 (practical limit), and we also enforce a 4MB total payload size cap. If either limit is hit we return 413 with a hint on how to chunk. Important: ordering guarantee — embeddings are returned in the same order the inputs were provided, even if we processed them in multiple compute batches.

megan: empty-string behavior: we canonicalize whitespace (trim) first. If the trimmed string is empty we return a deterministic zero-vector (all 0.0) of the model dimension (1536 for redwood-embed-3-small). If the client sends JSON null for an item we reject the request with 400 and the error code E_INVALID_INPUT — we do not emit a null embedding cell.

megan: small note on shape: response "embeddings" is a flat list aligned 1:1 with inputs. each embedding is an array of floats length 1536. example response snippet:
```json
{
  "embeddings": [
    [0.012, -0.003, ..., 0.001],
    [/* 1536 floats */],
    [0.0, 0.0, ..., 0.0]
  ]
}
```
(we avoid nested vectors for nested inputs — nested arrays are an error).

priya: got it. couple follow-ups: 1) how should SDKs surface the truncation so users aren't surprised when doc pieces get cut? 2) will we include the exact char cap in the response headers or a warning in the body?

jamal: good Q. plan is to: (a) add an X-Embed-Truncation header with the per-item char cap when truncation occurred for any item in the request, and (b) emit a lightweight warnings array in the response body listing which input indices were truncated. e.g., "warnings": [{"index": 1, "reason": "truncated_to_4096_chars"}]. I'll add this to the contract in the PR.

ci-bot: CI: PR #542 — unit/integration tests passed :white_check_mark: (build 3211)

alex: pinging @megan for docs update and @priya fyi for the SDK change. i'll file a follow-up task: ENGPLAT-771 documenting headers + sample warnings and update the JS/Python SDKs to coerce Buffer -> base64 string for binary inputs.

megan: I'll add a short section in the embeddings docs with examples for: mixed inputs, empty string behavior, sample warnings header, and error cases. also will add a small migration note for teams that relied on null-for-empty previously.

priya: perfect. small ask — can we also add a test case where an item is exactly 4096 chars to ensure off-by-one behavior is stable? i'll add it to PR 542 as a unit test.

jamal: yes please — that test is helpful. once CI is green i'll merge and cut a tiny changelog entry for the API contract.
